question: As reported in July 2025, what is the name of the new ultra-rare blood antigen discovered in a woman from the Kolar district of Karnataka?
solution:
The correct answer is __**CRIB**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **July 2025**, medical researchers identified a new ultra-rare blood antigen named **CRIB**.
 
• The discovery was made in a woman residing in the **Kolar district** of **Karnataka**, India.
 
• The identification of the **CRIB** antigen occurred during routine blood screening or cross-matching, where the patient's blood showed an unusual reaction that did not match existing known **blood group systems**.
 
• This finding is classified as **ultra-rare**, meaning it is found in an extremely small percentage of the global population, often making it difficult to find compatible **blood donors** for transfusions.
 
• The discovery highlights the genetic diversity within the Indian population and the importance of advanced **immunohematology** labs in detecting such rare phenotypes to ensure patient safety during medical procedures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Blood Antigens**: These are **proteins** or **sugars** located on the surface of **red blood cells**. They determine a person's blood type and trigger an immune response if incompatible blood is introduced into the body.
 
• **Rare Blood Groups in India**:
 
 
• **Bombay Blood Group (hh)**: First discovered in **1952** in **Mumbai** by **Dr. Y.M. Bhende**. It is found in roughly **1 in 10,000** individuals in India.
 
• **EMM Negative**: A rare blood group recently identified in **Gujarat** in **2022**. People with this type lack the **EMM antigen** on their red blood cells.
 
 
 
• **Rh-null (Golden Blood)**: This is considered the rarest blood type in the world, lacking all **61 antigens** in the **Rh system**. Since its discovery, fewer than **50 cases** have been reported globally.
 
• **International Society of Blood Transfusion (ISBT)**: This organization is responsible for the official classification of **blood group systems**. As of **2023-2024**, there are **45 recognized systems**, including **ABO**, **Rh**, **Kell**, and **Duffy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Transfusion Challenges**: Individuals with ultra-rare antigens like **CRIB** cannot receive blood from common donors (O, A, B, AB). They require blood from donors who also possess (or lack) the same specific antigen to avoid **hemolytic transfusion reactions**.
 
• **Genetic Mapping**: Regions like **Karnataka** and other parts of Southern India have shown unique **allelic frequencies** due to historical endogamy, leading to the discovery of several rare blood phenotypes.
 
• **Registry**: The **Indian Society of Blood Transfusion and Immunohaematology (ISBTI)** and various regional registries work to maintain databases of rare donors to assist in emergencies involving rare types like **CRIB**.
